116.desc: When the Rugrats overhear a mayoral candidate on television, they decide that Tommy is their mayor. Angelica insists that they must have an election, and she and Susie become "champagne managers" for Tommy and Phil respectively.

117.sub: Brothers Are Monsters / Cooking with Susie
117.desc: Oh, for peeps sake! Crawl on over for some pint-sized adventures in Rugrats Volume 5! Join the gang as they try and stay up through naptime, cure Tommy's baldness, and help Chuckie manage his newest fear--the carwash! Plus much more!

118.desc: Oh, for peeps sake! Crawl on over for some pint-sized adventures in Rugrats Volume 5! Join the gang as they try and stay up through naptime, cure Tommy's baldness, and help Chuckie manage his newest fear--the carwash! Plus much more!

119.sub: Planting Dil / The Joke's on You
119.desc: When the Rugrats hear that Didi is going to be "planting Dil" in her herb garden, they imagine a whole bunch of new baby Dil's. / Angelica sneaks around playing practical jokes on the Rugrats and sets up Dil as the scapegoat.

120.desc: When Angelica is forbidden to eat sweets at the park, she "kidnaps" Dil in her little car, and uses him to grab cookies from other parties, until the Rugrats chase after them, wanting to rescue Dil from a life of "crime.

121.desc: Didi introduces Goober, a goofy, gentle toy to Tommy and Dil as an antidote to the aggressive Reptar. Chuckie likes Goober, but Tommy does not. / When "Doctor" Susie fixes the Rugrats' broken toys, Angelica is jealous at all the attention Susie is getting.

122.desc: After Chuckie wets the bed one night, the Rugrats decide that Chuckie has to have a boring day so he won't have an exciting dream and forget to wake up and go potty. / After the Rugrats see home movies of Stu's scouting days, they decide to be scouts.

123.desc: When Chuckie rips his shirt, Chas buys him a new one, leading Chuckie to think he's not the same person and start going by the name "Ralph." / When Didi hides the cookie jar from Grandpa , Angelica convinces the babies to search for it.

124.desc: Chuckie has a nightmare in which the Rugrats have all shrunk to the size of his "little people" toys, except for Dil. / Angelica graduates from charm school and her newly-learned manners are put to the test when Charlotte hosts an important guest.

125.sub: A Dose of Dil / Famous Babies
125.desc: Tommy feels left out when everyone else is getting attention so he decides to try AngelicaÃ+s technique of pretending to be sick or hurt. In the end, Dil sees Tommy in distress and saves him.

126.desc: The babies and Angelica visit Susie in the hospital when she goes to get her tonsils removed. As Susie goes under, she dreams she has entered a strange, magical land, but she just wants to get home. She is joined by the Rugrats along the way.

127.desc: After Grandpa explains what Valentine's Day means to the babies, Angelica shoots Spike with Cupid's arrow. The babies decide they now have to find Spike a Valentine: Fluffy. Later that night, the families all attend a Valentine dance.

128.desc: When Aunt Miriam returns from a road trip across America, she forgets a Souvenir for Dil, and the babies search in their backyard for something suitable, going into fantasy at the Grand canyon, Everglades, Yellowstone, etc.

129.desc: Angelica warns the Rugrats the season of Fall is a time of change - and change ain't always good. When Grandpa Lou decides to move to the retirement community, the babies are afraid she's right.

130.desc: Angelica warns the Rugrats the season of Fall is a time of change - and change ain't always good. When Grandpa Lou decides to move to the retirement community, the babies are afraid she's right.

131.desc: The Rugrats try to stop Fall and its changes by stopping the Fall Festival parade, but it's Stu and his animatronic Reptar that bring everything to a halt.

132.sub: Angelicon / Dil's Binkie / Big Brother Chuckie
132.desc: Angelica turns into the giant creature of the jungle called "Angelicon". / When Dil's binkie pops out of his mouth, it takes a quick trip around the neighborhood. / Chuckie is afraid he'll never be a good "big brother".

133.sub: Dil Saver / Cooking with Phil & Lil / Piece of Cake
133.desc: Tommy is the victim of mistaken identity when a one-toothed baby who is dressed like him wreaks havoc on the kids at the park.

134.sub: Sister Act / Spike's Nightscare / Cuddle Bunny
134.desc: Angelica realizes she's the only one without a sibling and auditions each of the babies for the role. / When the babies see a sleeping Spike having a "nightscare," they try to help them through their nightmares. / Kimi falls in love with a donkey pinata.

135.desc: The new family of Finsters at home. After reading "Cinderella", Angelica tells Chuckie that he may have a mean step mommy.

136.sub: Bad Shoes / The World According to Dil & Spike / Falling Star
136.desc: Tommy and the babies save Stu from the world's most obstinate pair of shoes. / Tommy and Chuckie wonder what Dil and Spike think about / The babies hear there are going to be falling stars and "travel" into space.

137.sub: Dayscare / The Great Unknown / Wash Dry Story
137.desc: Tommy is rattled when he gets his first cut, but eventually learns that cuts do heal.

138.sub: Changes for Chuckie / The Magic Show / A Lulu of a Time
138.desc: With Kira and Kimi in his house, Chuckie sees changes everywhere and is sure life as he knew it is over. / Backstage at a magic show, the Rugrats discover real magic. / Lulu babysits the Rugrats at the retirement community.

139.sub: Cat Got Your Tongue? / The War Room / Attention Please
139.desc: Phil and Lil hear Lulu ask a hoarse Howard if the "cat's got his tongue" - they enlist the help of all the babies to hunt down Fluffy. / Tommy attempts to rescue Dil's bottle / Kira and Chas accidentally leave Chuckie feeling like the Odd Baby out.

140.sub: And the Winner Is... / Dil's Bathtime / Bigger Than Life
140.desc: Tommy Pickles and his pint-sized pals discover magic, danger and great comic adventure in a world we often take for granted. Tommy is joined by the twins Phil and Lil DeVille, his best friend Chuckie and Angelica, his three yea

141.sub: Day of the Potty / Tell-Tale Cell Phone / The Time of Their Lives
141.desc: During a visit to Home Wonderland, the babies become convinced an army of potties is after them. / Angelica accidentally breaks Charlotte's cell phone / When Kimi hides Angelica's watch, the Rugrats feel compelled to find it.

142.sub: My Fair Babies / The Way Things Work / Home Sweet Home
142.desc: Susie tries to make the babies into "growed-up kids". / Tommy explains life's inside to Dil. / When Chuckie fears Kimi's going to be mailed back to Japan, he and the other babies try to make her "last day" the best possible.

143.sub: Adventure Squad / The Way More Things Work / Talk of the Town
143.desc: Phil has increasing trouble tearing himself away from his favorite TV show, so the babies intervene. / Tommy explains life's backyard basics to Dil. / Angelica stages her version of a talk show, using it to find out who broke Kimi's new toy.

144.desc: When Aunt T. visits the Carmichaels to celebrate Kwanzaa, she tells Susie the holiday is a time to honor the legacy of our great people.

145.desc: Will Tommy still be the gang's fearless leader? Will Chuckie survive his first "crush"? Will Angelica still be underhanded? The answers are here as the entire Rugrats gang embarks on one of their most fantastic adventures yet.

146.desc: The rugrats travel ten years into the future where they experience life as young adults.

147.desc: Angelica and Susie break Miss Weemer's coffee mug. Then, along with Harold, they go on an adventure to repair the mug and realize that they make a good team.

148.desc: Angelica convinces the babies to give her their candy or they'll turn into whatever they dress up as. Chuckie finds his inner werewuff and stands up to Angelica.

149.desc: Tommy feels rejected when Spike seems to be paying all his attention to Fifi until the cause is revealed - Fifi delivers a doghouse full of puppies.

150.desc: Chuckie and Kimi get their own library cards on their 1st trip to the library. / Inspired by a visit to the old folk's home, Angelica schemes to get the babies to "tire".

151.sub: The Doctor Is In / The Big Sneeze
151.desc: As Betty and Didi listen to an abrasive Dr. Laura-type radio personality, Angelica decides this is a gig she was born for. / Angelica convinces Chuckie that he is allergic to Kimi because he has been sneezing every time she is around.

152.sub: The Fun Way Day / The Age of Aquarium
152.desc: In order to drum up more business, Kira hires a Feng Shui expert to rearrange the coffee shop. / The entire gang goes to the cheesy local aquarium for the day, which is shaped like a huge boat.

153.desc: When the mommies leave the babies with their fathers, all hell breaks loose at home. / Angelica tells the babies that the reason her new doll is so realistic is because it's actually a real baby that was turned into a doll.

154.desc: Chas and Kira take on a teen to help around the coffee shop. "Cyndy" is a dead ringer for Angelica's Cynthia doll. / In order to impress some four-year old girls with a "thing" for babies, Angelica promises to be nice to the Rugrats forever.

155.desc: To celebrate Boris and Minka's anniversary, the whole gang takes a train trip to Little Biendeltown, a theme-park re-creation of the Old Country. The scenic 18-hour journey is a send-up of Agatha Christie-style mysteries.

156.desc: When Didi decides to go "back to school", Angelica explains that soon Tommy will be a baby like Dil again. / Chas and Kira pursue their dream of owning a coffee shop while the Rugrats pursue their own dream - or, rather, Chuckie's dream.

157.sub: A Step at a Time / Angelica's Assistant
157.desc: The babies try and make Dil take his first steps so he can play a game with them. The adults - and the babies - reminiscence about each of the Rugrats' first steps. / Charlotte sets a play date for Angelica with bumbling pre-school classmate Harold.

158.sub: A Tale of Two Puppies / Okey-Dokey Jones and the Ring of the Sunbeams
158.desc: Chuckie decides to teach a puppy, "Puppy," to be brave so that she'll be adopted into a good home. / Grandpa Lou takes the babies to an exotic pet shop, and the babies go on an Indiana Jones type adventure to rescue Lil's ring from Angelica.

159.desc: The babies are worried that their new babysitter, a teen-angst wanna-be rocker named Taffy, is unhappy because she sings such sad songs. / Angelica coerces the Rugrats to take roles in her make-believe game based on her favorite TV show, "The Cynthia Team"

160.desc: The Rugrats discover that Christmas means more than just presents and tradition when they find themselves stranded in the Stu-inspired displays at a Christmas party.

161.desc: The Rugrats discover that Christmas means more than just presents and tradition when they find themselves stranded in the Stu-inspired displays at a Christmas party.

162.desc: Grandpa Lou convinces the entire gang that they need a vacation. When they arrive, the reservations have been screwed up: The parents are all forced to sleep in one room. The babies set off to find buried treasure and save their parents' vacation.

163.desc: Betty's English cousins come to visit America, bringing their perfectly mannered twins. Lil, feeling as if she and Phil are not living up to the "perfect twin" billing of her English cousins, tries to persuade Phil to be a perfect twin as well.

164.desc: When the babies are taken to the circus, Chuckie fears that he is turning into a clown. / When Angelica watches an award show on television, the babies decide to host their own 'rewards' show.

165.desc: The babies find a medieval themed arcade game that leads then into a fantasy to save Taffy from a fierce dragon named Gracko. / The babies try to make Dil stronger, so he can play with them, and after an earthquake strikes, they think he is responsible.

166.desc: Taffy takes the babies to their first high school basketball game, and they set out to defeat the visiting team's mascot. / Angelica convinces the babies that the Pickles' crawl space is their new play area so that she can have the living room to herself.

167.desc: Action star Mack Granite picks Kimi to audition for a part in his next movie. / When Taffy comes to baby-sit, but is in an artistic funk, and Angelica enters dressed (and acting) like Taffy, the babies think they've swapped identities.

168.sub: They Came from the Backyard / Lil's Phil of Trash
168.desc: When the TV signals keep getting switched, the babies think that 'aliums' are coming for them. / When Taffy takes the babies on a picnic in the park, Phil bonds with Dusty, a young "sanitation artist" picking up trash.

169.sub: Mutts in a Name / Hurricane Alice
169.desc: The Finster's puppy is lethargic, and the babies believe it's because she hasn't been properly named yet. / Betty's college roommate comes to visit with her daughter Alice, just as weather reports forecast a hurricane, also called Alice.

170.sub: Bestest of Show / Hold the Pickles
170.desc: Stu, Chas, Angelica, and Susie enter Spiffy, Puppy, Fluffy, and Herbie the gerbil, respectively, in a pet show, all vying for "Best Pet" honor. / Taffy takes the babies to their first fast food restaurant.

171.desc: When the babies accompany their mothers to Krudnik's annual half-off baby sale, the Rugrats think that they are being sold. / The babies build a snowbaby and name him Steve.

172.desc: Tommy temporarily loses his nerve after slipping on a playground apparatus, and Angelica challenges the babies to tests of valor to see who's the "braveliest". / Didi takes the babies to college to be part of her Child Development experiment.

173.sub: Fountain of Youth / Kimi Takes the Cake
173.desc: Stu, Drew, and Chas take their families to Lake Crackaknee, where they spent their childhood vacations. / For Kimi's first birthday with the Finsters, her parents have arranged a special party at Happy Castle.

the busy world of richard scarry.display: The Busy World of Richard Scarry

1.sub: The Talking Bread / Couscous, the North African Detective / The Three Fishermen
1.desc: Sergeant Murphy's got his hands full with runaway imaginations. / Couscous is the best detective in North Africa and he's on the trail of Pepe Le Gangster and his "dirty rats."Father Cat takes Huckle and Lowly on their first fishing trip hoping it will be as magical as his own.

2.sub: The Best Birthday Present Ever / Patrick Pig Learns to Talk / Grouchy Mr. Gronkle
2.desc: Huckle and Lowly buy a special cuckoo clock for Mother Cat, but because Huckle's bike bell doesn't work, he has an accident and the cuckoo clock breaks. Despite his talkative Irish forefathers, Patrick O'Swine can't utter a word. The gang goes skating on Grouchy Mr. Gronkle's pond, and when the old koot sees them on his property, he hurries to shoo them away.

3.sub: The Busiest Firefighters Ever / Manuel of Mexico / The Biggest Catch Ever
3.desc: Huckle and Lowly keep missing the Big Stories around town. / Pepe and his gang of Dirty Rats escape from prison. / Mr. Frumble volunteers to help around the fire station.

4.sub: Mr. Raccoon's Different Day / Mario, the Venetian Gondolier / The Best Babysitter Ever
4.desc: Mr. Raccoon is bored with the same old thing everyday so he leaves Mr. Frumble in charge of his restaurant while he goes in search of a change. / Mario wants a gondola so he can paddle romantic couples around Venice, but instead he owns a big clunky melon boat. / Hilda babysits for Pig Will and Pig Won't and she does her best to fill the day with fun, but Pig Won't just wants to sulk.

5.sub: The Best Mistake Ever / Sneef, the Best Detective in Europe / Camping Out
5.desc: Huckle's off to do Mother Cat's shopping for the first time when he forgets the list. / The Police Chief gives urgent orders to Sneef and his assistant Sniff - they must hurry to Nice. / Huckle and Lowly camp in the backyard but after Kenny tells them a ghost story, they're sure they see a huge claw in the shadows.

6.sub: Mr. Frumble's New Cars / Ernst and Heidi in the Alps / Billy Dog's Bad Day
6.desc: When Mr. Frumble crashes his car he steals the bulldozer from Roger Rhino, a taxi and the airplane from Rudolph Von Flugel, Ernst and Heidi from the Swiss alps are introduced and Billy Dog has a bad day.

7.sub: The Snowstorm / Professor Dig and His Egyptian Mummy / The Treasure Hunt
7.desc: A big snowstorm causes havoc in Busytown, Professor Dig is introduced with his own Egyptian mummy and a treasure hunt takes place in Busytown.

8.sub: The Missing Bananas / Good Luck in Rome / The Accident
8.desc: The traffic light Mr. Fixit 'fixed' causes a big pile up so he offers to repair all the cars. The drivers decide to repair the cars themselves and a hurt Mr. Fixit locks himself in his shop. No one can fix things like Mr. Fixit, and soon everyone's pleading for his help. Fixit grabs his hammer and the cars are rebuilt better - and different - than before. Maria and Frederico want to throw a coin in the Trevi fountain for luck. They get lost, Maria falls asleep, and Frederico breaks a Roman statue which he puts in the car. The car drives off with the statue at the wheel - and Frederico in pursuit - and it stops in the Trevi fountain. Maria and Frederico will get lots of luck now - instead of a coin, they threw in their whole car. Bananas offers to watch Turnip Goat's bananas while she unloads her truck. When the bunch disappears, Bananas Gorilla panics. Huckle and Lowly help him track down the bananas, and they get them back before Turnip even noticed they were gone. Bananas even gets a banana reward for his trouble.

9.sub: A Trip to the Moon / Pip Pip Goes to London / Floating Bananas
9.desc: Huckle, Lowly, the Three Beggars and Mr. Frumble are accidentally launched to the moon in Mr. Fixit's home made rocket. The landing on the moon is less than smooth, and the rocket breaks. Our astronauts manage to repair the rocket and it's back to Earth for a hero's welcome and some lunch. Pip Pip comes to London hoping to work for the Queen. With her new friend, Liza Littlemouse, they go to the palace, the Navy, and then the Tower of London, but no luck. When the Queen loses her ring, Pip Pip and Liza find it in a fountain and the Queen makes them the royal fountain keepers. Bananas wants to buy bananas so he hurries to the harbour hoping to work on the banana cargo ship that's in port. Sergeant Murphy sees banana peels in the harbor and suspects that Bananas has stolen the cargo. But Bananas did get a job - as a chef - and when the mess is cleaned up, everyone has some of his banana soup.

10.sub: Hat Pie / Hans, the Dutch Plumber / Hilda's Romantic Tea Party
10.desc: After Sally, Lowly, and Huckle help Mother Cat make an apple pie, Lowly's yodeler hat is missing. Lowly and Huckle team up with the missing hat expert, Mr. Frumble, and they look high and low but can't find Lowly's hat anywhere. When everyone finally sits down to enjoy the apple pie, Mr. Frumble finds the hat - in the 'hat' pie. Hans loves plumbing but because he always comes home wet, his wife takes him to apply for a dry windmill keeper's job. On the way, Hans plugs a hole in a dike and saves the town. He gets a medal and a new job - Chief Plumber. Now Hans can still be a plumber but he won't get wet - that is if he stops driving his bike into the canals. Hilda plays matchmaker for Bruno and Ms. Honey by planning a wonderful tea party. When the day is less than perfect, Hilda is certain she's failed. Especially when on the river boat trip, Bruno has to rescue Lowly. But Ms. Honey is charmed and impressed by Bruno's courage, and Hilda smiles as the two go off arm-in-arm!

11.sub: A Big Operation / Cucumber, the African Photographer / Summer Picnic
11.desc: When Huckle has to get his tonsils out, Lowly stays with him in the hospital. / Cucumber and her assistant Pickles are terrified of their new assignment - to get pictures of lions. / All the kids and Miss Honey go up river for a picnic.

12.sub: Sergeant Murphy's Day Off / Schmudge, the German Chimney Sweep / The Sleeping Car Adventure
12.desc: Sergeant Murphy gets his first day off, Schmudge a chimney Sweeper in Germany is introduced and Hilda takes a train ride.

13.sub: Busytown Regatta / Schtoompah, the Funny Austrian / Busytown Soap Box Derby
13.desc: Knights and a bucketman are a major occurrence in Busytown and the life of cave pigs is featured.

14.sub: The Big Story / Couscous in Gibraltar / The Firefighter's Ball
14.desc: Huckle and Lowly keep missing the Big Stories around town as they go after a scoop for the school newspaper. / Pepe and his gang of Dirty Rats escape from prison and look for a boat in Gibraltar to get far away. / Mr. Frumble volunteers to help around the fire station, and he's a little disappointed when all he's to do is decorate for the annual Fireman's Ball.

15.sub: The Field Trip / The Great Pie Robbery / Clean Garage
15.desc: Sprout Goat's really disappointed when he can't go on a field trip to the Hydro-Electric plant with Sergeant Murphy - he's got to help his father harvest the tomatoes. There's been a terrible theft in Paris - Madame Dog's famous pies have been stolen and Sam and Dudley are called in. After Father Cat smashes his headlight on some junk in the garage, Huckle and Lowly help him clean up once and for all.

16.sub: Captain Willy and the Pirates / Flying Noodles / Roughing It
16.desc: A class lesson comes to life as Huckle and his classmates learn about the Olden Days of Busy Town: when Captain Willy took on a gang of mouse pirates who steal his lunch. Cucumber and Pickles arrive in Japan to take pictures of the famous noodle maker Chef Sato, but when he goes missing, they head out to find him. / Mr. Fixit takes the scouts camping to rough it in the wilds, but his idea of roughing it isn't the same as what the Scouts have in mind.

17.sub: Young Vikings / Sneef Saves the Queen / Hilda the Director
17.desc: Huckle, Lowly, and Sally decide to build a raft. / On a royal trip to Australia, the Queen's jewels go missing. / A magazine article inspires Hilda and she decides to direct her own play.

18.sub: High Flyers / Steamboat Mystery / The Best Waiters Ever
18.desc: Rudolph Von Flugel takes Huckle and Lowly up in his airplane, but he forgets to do up his own seatbelt. / The Pigs celebrate their anniversary by throwing a costume party on a Lake Geneva steamboat. Mayor Fox has invited the Mayor of Workville to dine with him at Louie's restaurant.

19.sub: The Big Move / Sneef in Russia / Mr. Frumble Gets a Job
19.desc: Huckle, Lowly and Billy Dog are having fun playing around at the Busytown observatory where Billy's mom works, but the fun ends when she tells Billy their moving. Sneef and Sniff arrive in Russia to guard a diamond framed painting which is being transported by train. After being helped himself, Mr. Frumble decides to get a job helping other people.

20.sub: Ambulance Cake / The Supermarket Mystery / Big Trouble for Bananas Gorilla
20.desc: Everyone in Busytown's getting ready for the big Hospital bake sale, and Mother Cat's made her famous cake. Detectives Sam and Dudley are called upon to find out who's stealing groceries at the big Los Angeles supermarket. Gorilla: It's Bananas Gorilla's first day on the job at Scotty's garage and boy does it start off bad.

21.sub: Sergeant Murphy's Deputy / Couscous in the Sahara / New Friend on the Block
21.desc: Overworked Sgt. Murphy gets "help" from a deputy just out of the academy. Pepe le Gangstaire and his Dirty Rats escape from prison to steal the Jewel of Jewels from a passing caravan. Huckle and Lowly are hurrying out the door when Mother Cat asks them to deliver cookies to the new family on the block.

22.sub: The Biggest Storm Ever / Cucumber in Rockies / Sally's First Day at School
22.desc: Sally Cat starts kindergarten, Cucumber manages to stop a runaway boxcar that is carrying a wedding cake in the Canadian rockies and a big storm occurs in Busytown.

23.sub: No Time for Bananas / Sneef in India / Sally Cat's First Trip
23.desc: There's a big show in town, and Bananas Gorilla gets a crush on Ms. Coconut, the lead actress. The nefarious jewel thief Lady Cheetah strikes again when disguised as the Royal Fortune Teller she steals all of Prince Tusk's jewels. Sally Cat is going on a trip all by herself to Sand Dollar Beach to visit her cousin Lily... and she's going to fly there in a plane.

24.sub: Grand Hotel / Couscous on the Nile / Cat Family Ski Trip
24.desc: Father Cat is supposed to review the Grand Hotel for his travel agency, but as soon as he gets there, he sprains his ankle. Pepe and his Dirty Rats are out of jail, and disguised as humble servants, they are robbing the Empress of Fazooly blind. Father Cat wants the family to spend more time together, so they all go on a ski trip.

25.sub: Lowly Breaks His Leg / Cucumber in Machuu Pichuu / The Plight of Penelope Parakeet
25.desc: While climbing a tree to get Huckle a juicy apple, Lowly falls and breaks his leg. The day Cucumber and Pickles arrive in Machu Pichu to photograph the 10 golden rings, some are stolen... and Cucumber and Pickles are blamed. Huckle and Lowly are going to pet-sit Hilda's pet parakeet Penelope, but when the little bird gets loose, Huckle and Lowly scramble to catch it before Hilda gets back.

26.sub: A Newspaper Mom / Cucumber in Rio / Donut Raffle
26.desc: To earn money to buy a stereo system, Huckle get a job delivering newspapers. It's the big Rio Carnival and Cucumber and Pickles are there to capture everything on film... except that everything isn't much - all the costumes are missing. Humperdink the baker is raffling off 100 donuts and everyone in town is buying a ticket.

27.sub: The Knights of Busytown / Cave Pigs / Play It Safe!
27.desc: A game of Knights of the Busytown Round Table ends when Sally doesn't want to be the fair maiden in distress anymore. She decides to build her own castle in the Cat family's backyard, while Huckle and Lowly build one too. Then when Hilda suggests they combine both castles to make a big one, all the kids get to play together and the fair maiden is none other than Hilda Hippo. / Bump and Thump are inventors from pre-historic times, and on this busy day they come up with great ways to make life easier for the Cave Pigs. But when the Cave Pigs don't appreciate the first house, or the first dinner table and plates, Bump and Thump fear they've failed... that is until our great inventors combine all that day's failures and make the first ever wagon. Now this is the kind of fun Cave Pigs love. / Mr. Frumble buys a new TV antennae but his attempts to get better reception land him stuck in a paint-splattered garbage can and looking like a 'Bucketman From Outer Space'. He causes panic in Busytown until Huckle and Lowly see him in danger and hurry to help. They rescue Mr. Frumble and even help him get perfect TV reception.

28.sub: Billy Dog Gets Glasses / Cordelia's Debut / Lowly Joins the Circus
28.desc: Billy Dog gets his own glasses for the first time, Cordelia debuts and Lowly Worm takes part in a circus.

29.sub: The Big Dare / Oliver's Sandwich / Pig Will Won't
29.desc: A big dare takes place, Oliver gets problems with his sandwich and Pig Will and Pig Won't are introduced.

30.sub: The Best Birthday Party Ever / Martha's First Book / Locked Out
30.desc: A big birthday party takes place in Busytown, Martha reads her first book and one gets locked out.

31.sub: Dad's Neat Job / The Discovery of America / Mr Gronkle's Friends
31.desc: Father Cat does a new job, the story of America being discovered is featured and Mr. Grankle's friends are introduced.

32.sub: Denys at Camp / Peasant Pig's Gifts / Little Fixit
32.desc: Denys go to camp, Peasant Pig gets his own gifts and Little Fixit, the sister of Mr. and Mrs. Fixit is introduced.

33.sub: The School Dance / The First Olympics / Hilda for President
33.desc: A school dance takes place, The story of the Greek Olympics is featured and Hilda takes president.

34.sub: Mr. Frumble's Brother / Viking Pigs / The Perfect Wedding
34.desc: Mr. Frumble's brother is introduced, the Viking pigs are introduced and a wedding takes place in Busytown.

35.sub: A Tough Test / The First Pyramid / The Big Date
35.desc: A tough test takes place, the story of the discovery of the first pyramid is featured and a big date takes place.

36.sub: Inventor of the Year / Macaroni Polo / Lone Wolf at the Lighthouse
36.desc: One of Busytown's residents gets an award for being the inventor of the year, Macaroni Polo is introduced and Lone Wolfe is at a lighthouse.

37.sub: Fun-Time Riddle Race / The First Balloon / Billy Dog's Space Rock
37.desc: A big riddle race takes place in Busytown starting at the Fire station (with the riddle "When things get really hot, we'll bring you some water") and ending at the Observatory (with the riddle "When it gets dark, look up and watch the show"), the story of the first balloon (a.k.a. Montgolfier) is featured and Billy Dog loses a meteorite from the observatory and tries to find and return it.

38.sub: The Best Amusement Park Ever / The First Bridge / Say Cheese Please!
38.desc: Wolfgang, Benny and Harry open a big amusement park, but having trouble in the process, the story of the first bridge is featured (caused by a toppling tower that lands on the river) and the class has to take photos of their families, but experiencing many problems and Huckle finally succeeds in taking the best picture.

39.sub: Has Anyone Seen My Book? / PJ Pig's Brave Day / Vanderbuilt's New Shoes
39.desc: A book goes missing, P.J. Pig does his best and Vanderbuilt gets new shoes.

40.sub: The Perfect Gentleman / The Best Painter Ever / The Best Day for Dennis
40.desc: A new gentleman comes, a painter does some amazing work and Dennis has his best day.

41.sub: A Trip Back in Time / Home Sweet Home / P.S. Pig's Special Friend
41.desc: A trip back in time takes place and P.S. Pig gets a new friend.

42.sub: Mr. Fixit's Magnet Machine / Sneef and Sniff at the Opera / Mr. Gronkle Won't Mind
42.desc: Mr. Fixit causes havoc with his new magnet machine that gets out of control and attracts anything made of metal, Sniff and Sneef solve a voice problem at a European Opera and an eventful day occurs in the lives of Lowly, Huckle, and Father Cat.

43.sub: Peter's Visit / The First Skis Ever / Stage Fright
43.desc: Peter visits, the story of the first skis takes place and some stage fright occurs.

44.sub: End of the Rainbow / A Signal for Peng / Mr. Frumble's Birthday Party
44.desc: The kindergarten class loves the story about a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow. Peng's wife, Mei, is about to have a baby when Peng gets a job at the Great Wall of China. When Mr. Frumble sees a pile of unmailed invitations on his kitchen table, he remembers it's his birthday and he's throwing himself a birthday party.

45.sub: Bananas the Magician / The First Horseless Carriage / Princess Hilda
45.desc: Bananas Gorilla decides to become a magician, but after only one day of practicing he gives up. To boost his confidence, Huckle and Lowly make one of his tricks work, and Bananas the Magnificent's fame spreads through Busytown. Bananas decides to do his biggest trick ever, and when it fails, Huckle and Lowly must tell him the truth - Bananas Gorilla is plain ol? Bananas, and that's just fine with him. / Every week Nicholas Cugnot and his family push their heavy cart up a steep hill to the village market, much to the amusement of all the other villagers. So, when the family discovers that steam can move things, they invent the first ever steam carriage. The villagers are amazed with this new invention, but the Cugnots forgot one small detail on the carriage? BREAKS! / When "professional actress" Hilda Hippo doesn't get the lead role in the school play, her dreams of fame are shattered. Hilda's sure all she needs is a break, and boy does she get it. Hilda finds herself all alone on the "Cooking in Busytown" set at the Busytown Broadcasting Center, and she has a field day cooking up a storm, while all her friends tune in for the funny show.

46.sub: Daylight Savings Time / Eager Beaver's Clever Game / The Pickle Car Wash
46.desc: The story of Daylight Savings Time is featured, Eager Beaver makes a clever game and Mr. Frumble has his own car wash for his Pickle Car.

47.sub: Triple a Deliveries / Stanley's Amazing Photo / Lost in the Swamp
47.desc: Stanley does some of the best photographing and one gets lost in the swamp.

48.sub: Mr. Fixit's Super Submarine / Cahuchu's Magic Tree / Mr Bean's Restaurant
48.desc: Mr. Fixit invents a submarine and Lowly and Huckle give it a test ride, Little Cahuchu discovers a tree with magical bouncing sap and Mr. Bean opens a drive-in restaurant.

49.sub: Abe and Babe's Christmas Lesson / Sally Cat's Christmas Dream / The Best Christmas Present Ever
49.desc: A big Christmas present comes to Busytown, Abe and Babe get a Christmas lesson and Sally Cat gets her Christmas Dream.

50.sub: The Best Car Trip Ever / Earnest's Dish You Can Eat / Cousin Ross
50.desc: The Cat family goes on a big car trip, Earnest introduces his dish you can eat and cousin Ross is introduced.

51.sub: Fill'er Up Scotty / Niagara Falls Mystery / Helper's Helper
51.desc: Scotty operates a gas station, Cucumber succeeds a mystery when Niagara Falls stops flowing and it is blocked by Beaver Sweet Tooth's gang and one helper gets another helper.

52.sub: Who's Afraid of the Big Eclipse / Hold Your Breath! / Pumpkin Heads
52.desc: When there is a misprint in The Bugle, the townspeople think that the sun will disappear for 360 years, Toula and her father catch a gold necklace in their net and Huckle, Lowly and Sprout participate in a pumpkin contest.

53.sub: The Mole Machine / The Royal Game of Dennis / Now That's Progress
53.desc: Dennis gets a royal game and progress takes place, Mr. Fixit invents a mole machine.

54.sub: Superstitious Bananas / Pépé le Gangstaire / Drive-Through Movie
54.desc: Bananas Gorilla gets his superstitious bananas and a drive-through theater opens.

55.sub: King and Queen for a Day / The Piggy Express / Practice Makes Perfect
55.desc: A delighted Hilda, and a not so delighted Huckle are chosen as King and Queen. Piggy delivers mail through some stormy weather. There is a school recital and everyone is unhappy with their parts.

56.sub: The Winners / No More Games, Manuel! / We Won't Go to the Doctor!
56.desc: There's going to be a big race in Busytown, and the first prize is a neato bike-and everyone wants to win, so much so that the competition in Busytown gets a little too fierce. Little Manuel and his lively imagination are back as he and Pedro play jungle explorers. Pig Will and Pig Won't have their ideas about what happens when you go to the doctor's.

57.sub: Never Too Small / Albert, the Belgian Barge Captain / Rainy Day
57.desc: Sally and Robbie are too small to play basketball. There is a festival of giants in Belgium. Huckle, Lowly and Sally are bored on a rainy day.

58.sub: Mr. Gronkle Comes to Stay / Leo-pardo's Smile / Blooming Busytown
58.desc: Mr. Gronkle stays with the Cat family during winter, but freezes in the ice, Leo-pardo smiles for the first time and flowers are blooming all over Busytown.

59.sub: Match-Makers / Forget-bur Never Forgets / Toof Trouble
59.desc: Huckle plays matchmaker for Mr. Frumble. In Mesopotamia before writing is invented, Forget-bur tries to build a Ziggurat but keeps forgetting his plans. Hilda has a toothache but is in denial.

60.sub: The New Neighbors / The First Halloween Ever / Now I Know My One, Two, Threes!
60.desc: A new neighbor moves into the spooky house. The story of the 1st Halloween is told. Sally learns how to count and realizes it's okay to ask for help.

61.sub: Mr. Gronkle Moves Away / Counting Chickens / The Spelling Bee
61.desc: Mr. Gronkle moves to the quieter countryside. Before numbers are invented, a scribe must take inventory. Billy enters a spelling bee but lacks confidence in his abilities.

62.sub: Huckle's Feathery Friends / The First Valentine Ever / The Sleepover
62.desc: Huckle knocks over a bird's nest. The first valentine is featured. Dennis goes to Sprout's sleepover.

63.sub: Count on Us! / The First Easter Egg Ever / Be My Valentine
63.desc: There's a bikeathon, but Billy needs a bike. A family promises to give their king a gift. It's Valentine's Day and Hilda gets carried away.

64.sub: The Mystery of the Stone Circle / The Big Apple Christmas Caper / Who's Too Scared to Masquerade?
64.desc: A substitute takes the class to the Stone Circle. On Christmas, someone tries to rob the city. Little kids get intimidated by a masquerade party.

65.sub: A Message in a Bottle / Santa Needs Help / There Really Is an Easter Bunny
65.desc: Huckle discovers a message in a bottle with an SOS. Hilda writes her Christmas story. Everyone except Huckle is excited for the Easter egg hunt.

1.sub: Stimpy's Big Day! / The Big Shot!
1.desc: Stimpy wins a competition that takes him to the Big-time in Hollywood. Ren, left at home, begins to miss Stimpy more than he ever would have thought. Will Stimpy, rich and successful, remember Ren and return home?

2.desc: Ren Hoëk becomes "Robin Hoëk" in this parody of the Robin Hood legend. Stimpy, however, runs from scene to scene as he takes on the role of every other character. Next, stricken with an illness, Ren is brought back to health through Stimpy's unusual nursing practices. In some cases, the cure can be worse than the illness!

3.sub: Space Madness / The Boy Who Cried Rat!
3.desc: On their journey through space, Ren and Stimpy find that the true danger is "Space Madness", a cabin-crazy condition that Ren succumbs to. Next, in a sick tribute to classic animation, the two cook up a ploy to act as a rodent removal service. Ren becomes the mouse, and Stimpy as the cat. They take their services to suburbia with mixed results.

4.desc: On the brink of starvation, and disguised as Dalmatians, the pair find employment at a fire station. Can these two handle an inferno at a towering skyscraper, with all of its exotic residents in need of rescue? Next, Stimpy, a little giant, and the brunt of the big giants' jokes, leaves home to find a happier life. What partnership will unfold when he meets Ren, a simple dairy farmer?

5.desc: After a crash-landing on a strange planet, Commander Hoek and Cadet Stimpy go about cataloging and reporting on the strange planets inhabitants. But, before long, and quite unexpectedly, an inhabitant takes a very close look at them. Next, in kitsch documentary style, Ren narrates over some footage of curious flora and fauna. Finally, we are treated to a rare spotting of the Crocostimpy.

6.desc: Commander Hoek and Cadet Stimpy are sucked into the hideous vortex of a black hole. Now as inhabitants on a new planet, and constantly mutating, the pair solve an age-old mystery after being tipped-off by a familiar smell. Next, Stimpy in his naive optimism, invents an emotion-controlling helmet. Ren, whether he likes it or not, is now the involuntary test-subject.

7.desc: Ren and Stimpy join the Army, where they begin basic training under a very demanding Drill Sargent. We then follow the unusual and bizarre adventures of "Powdered Toast Man" as he is called on for various rescue missions.

8.desc: Ren learns the benefits of dental hygiene the hard way, as he refuses to listen to Stimpy's advice on brushing your teeth. Then Ren and Stimpy are tossed in the pound, where they discover the true meaning of "going to sleep".

9.desc: Ren and Stimpy find themselves amid the Wild West, where they run up against a Sheriff and Deputy who's favourite past-time is hanging people. They then hit the road as salesmen, going door-to-door to sell Rubber Nipples.

10.desc: Ren is excited when his cousin, Svën, is coming over for a visit, until he finds out that Svën is an idiot just like Stimpy.

11.desc: Convinced that wrestling is all an act, Mad Dog Höek (Ren) and Killer Kodoogan (Stimpy) are thrown into the wrestling ring for a bout against the enormous Lout Brothers, Lump and Loaf. Next, we see the Ren and Stimpy spend "the next twelve minutes" inside a mansion haunted by a shy, depressed and thoroughly non-scary Casper-like ghost.

12.desc: Ren & Stimpy, starving, exploit the benefits of living as babies. Then, George Liquor American takes us the Dog Show, where Ren & Stimpy are pitted against some tough competition. But only George can handle the judge's harsh scrutiny.

13.desc: One of Stimpy's bodily functions literally has a life of it's own in this episode. His flatulence becomes like the son he never had. Ghostlike and helpless, it wanders the streets looking for a home but finds the world harsh and careless. Grieving at his loss, and ceaselessly searching for his long lost "Stinky", Stimpy becomes a preoccupied and worried mess. Will the two meet again in a heart-warming reunion?

14.sub: Monkey See, Monkey Don't / Fake Dad
14.desc: In another scheme to feed and shelter themselves for free, the pair approach a zoo keeper disguised as monkeys. Will they take on the habits of the crude, resident chimp, or is the simian lifestyle too grotesque even for Ren and Stimpy? Next, Ren adopts a huge, violent inmate as a son for the weekend. Can Stimpy keep Ren's short-tempered parenting style under control, or will the lumbering, childish step son (Kowalski) find a place in Ren's heart?

15.sub: The Great Outdoors / The Cat That Laid the Golden Hairball
15.desc: Camping at a lakeside wood, Ren and Stimpy go about making a pleasant camping trip. Faced with dehydrated food, mosquito squadrons and eccentric skinny dippers, the great outdoors shows that it has it's share of challenges for the pair. Next, Ren exploits Stimpy's hairball habit upon hearing the price of this rare commodity soar. A production line (featuring Kowalksi as a laborer) is where Ren extracts the over-priced and disgusting fur from his swiftly balding friend Stimpy.

16.desc: Ren's jealousy drives him to distraction when day after day, the mailman dumps mountains of fan mail addressed to Stimpy only. Stimpy appeases Ren's feelings of worthlessness by appointing him president of the Official Stimpy Fan Club. Can Ren put his feelings aside in order to perform the delicate duties involved in receiving and replying to the inexhaustible stream of Stimpy's fan mail?

17.desc: Ren and Stimpy visit a young fan at his home.

18.desc: The pioneering spirit is abound in this re-telling of the colonization of the north American continent. With the motto "We Always Get Our Butts Kicked!", Ren and Stimpy set out across forests, deserts, mountains and vast snow fields atop lumbering yaks. Can they tap into the nation's vast natural resources to bring about prosperity?

19.sub: To Salve and Salve Not! / A Yard Too Far
19.desc: Capitalising on Stimpy's idiocy, a door-to-door salesman makes a nuisance of himself as he continually appears in surprising places to pressure Stimpy to buy his Salve product. Next, Stimpy is worried when he discovers that he has no pants to wear, and embarks on a grand mission through city and country to attain some.

20.desc: In a classic Hanna and Barbera tribute, Ren and Stimpy follow their noses to the ultimate free lunch: a dish of hog jowls cooling on a window-sill. Can they reach this treat, or will the resident baboon, napping in the yard, pose a mortal threat? Next, hitch-hiking in the middle of nowhere, the two are picked-up by a disturbing duo of maniacal midgets intent on causing chaos, crime and vaudevillian behavior.

21.desc: The first half of this episode sees Ren, after a humiliating experience at the beach, electing to have some pectoral implants. Can Stimpy, his kind donor, keep up with Ren's new lifestyle? Next, the two respond to a job vacancy guarding the Lincoln memorial. Will they succeed, while under the watchful eye of a transvestite Army Officer, in finding a mythical treasure hidden inside the very statue they guard?

22.desc: Stimpy draws an animated cartoon to show to his idol, Wilbur Cobb, while Ren serves as a producer on the project.

23.desc: Stimpy tries to remedy Ren's nasty behavior by introducing him to his conscience. Ren's conscience is played by the great guitar playing oaf, Jiminy Lummox.

24.desc: Ren's feeling fine on his 10th birthday until Stimpy reminds him that he's 70 years old in "dog years". Ren prepares for death with a will, a fake funeral, and the search for the perfect coffin.

25.sub: Jerry the Bellybutton Elf / Road Apples
25.desc: Stimpy becomes so obsessed with playing with his belly button that he ends up inside of it; Ren and Stinpy pretend to be roadkill in the desert.

26.desc: TV star Haggis MacHaggis (voiced by Alan Young) is kicked out of his mansion and thrown out onto the streets after Ren and Stimpy's cartoon show becomes more popular than his. Just as he plans to end it all, Haggis enlists in the help of two thugs-for-hire who help him sabotage Ren and Stimpy's show.

27.sub: Eat My Cookies / Ren's Bitter Half
27.desc: Desperate to join the Barrette Beret Girls, Ren and Stimpy have to prove themselves to the burly babes. When Ren gets hold of Stimpy's cloning liquid, he splits into 2 Rens.

28.desc: In this wildlife documentary, Ren and his stupid assistant observe the natural behavior of the rare animal called the Lummox. Actually an obese, ignorant, dim-witted and unhygienic human, these massive land-beasts exhibit playfulness, curiosity, rage and most intriguing of all, courtship. Which of the two competing ignoramuses underpants has what it takes to win over the female of the species?

29.desc: Stimpy's stupidity becomes too much for Ren and he leaves home to become a hermit. All alone, Ren begins to go crazy because he misses his true friend.

30.sub: House of Next Tuesday / A Friend in Your Face!
30.desc: Ren and Stimpy spend some time in a flawed futuristic house; Ren and Stimpy have parasitic creatures living in their heads annoying Ren immensely.

31.desc: Stimpy is becoming dangerously stupid. Ren is injected into his body in a race against time to find the problem. / When Ren and Stimpy try to collect money from their paper route, Pierre convinces them to grow up and get a man's job - lumberjacking.

32.desc: Ren & Stimpy go to the Natural History Museum to see the skeletal remains of the mammoth Stimpysaurus. Wilbur Cobb tells them about the evolution of the great beast and says that even the meat-eating Renosaurus couldn't conquer the huge bumbling idiot.

33.sub: Magical Golden Singing Cheeses / Hard Day's Luck
33.desc: Renwaldo sends Stimpleton on a food mission to trade their last chigger for some cheese. Stimpy meets a village idiot and trades his chigger for the magical golden singing cheeses.

34.sub: I Love Chicken / Powdered Toast Man vs. Waffle Woman
34.desc: In a deranged tribute to the "I Love Lucy" show, Stimpy lavishes affection on a store-bought oven-ready chicken. Next, Powdered-Toast Man and Waffle-Woman face off in a fight-to-the-death; the world hangs in the balance.

35.desc: It's the 11th hour at the dog pound and Ren and Stimpy are about to take that last long walk. A sweet rich old lady falls for them and adopts them immediately.

36.sub: Double Header / The Scotsman in Space
36.desc: This great star of a kiddy TV show is quickly overshadowed by the new cult hit "The Ren & Stimpy Show." The Scotsman kidnaps Ren & Stimpy in a rage.

37.desc: Ren and Stimpy find themselves in elf and gnome world where everyone happily works to graduate Pixie status. Stimpy loves his new work, but Ren thinks it's too hard and everyone is too happy. Ren decides instead that he wants to become a pixie king.

38.desc: Ren becomes insomniac. My Shiny Friend: Stimpy becomes addicted to television.

39.desc: Ren & Stimpy journey to the Blue-Cheese Mountains to become miners. After dealing with some savages, they finally reach the blessed mountains where they mine the cheese and dream of being rich.

40.desc: Wilbur Cobb tells a campfire story about Galoot Wranglers. Ren and Stimpy play the part of the galoot wranglers. / Ren goes crazy and is sent to a home. Here we see the whole cast of the Ren & Stimpy show has gone nuts.

41.desc: Slap on your Happy Helmets with everyone?s favorite psychotic Chihuahua and stupid cat in these classic episodes.

42.sub: Ol' Blue Nose / Stupid Sidekick Union
42.desc: Stimpy's newfound talent for crooning makes him famous. Stimpy's union goes on strike and Ren is forced to find a new sidekick.

43.desc: Ren and Stimpy are going to be the first dog and cat sent up to space in the Russian space program. / In the spirit of the Hatfields and McCoys, Ren and Stimpy present the Nitwits and the Dimwits.

44.sub: Hair of the Cat / City Hicks
44.desc: Ren is suffering from horrible allergies. Little does he know that he may be allergic to his best pal Stimpy.

45.desc: Ren and Stimpy find an abandoned circus clown at their doorstep. While Ren DOES NOT want to keep him, Stimpy pleads and begs until Ren agrees. Ren's status as Lord of the Manor is challenged. / Stimpy the mad scientist replaces Ren's brain.

46.desc: Ren and Stimpy get jobs as bellhops and must make sure that no one finds out who is living in the top two floors of the hotel, but their curiosity gets the best of them. Mark Hamill voices Mr. Noggin. / Ren is getting ready for the annual Dog Lodge meeting and Stimpy begs to come along (due to the fact that the lodge is for dogs only since he's a cat) in which Ren agrees to bring him to the Dog Lodge. However, this turns out to be a mistake by letting his feline friend to Dog Lodge and the two dogs refusing Ren to join in the lodge by thinking that he is some type of a different animal such as a mosquito. And so, the two dogs are having Ren to do a traditional dog test to prove to them that he is a canine.

47.sub: I Was a Teenage Stimpy / Who's Stupid Now?
47.desc: Stimpy enters his teens; the pair's show is canceled.

48.desc: Ren's old school friend visits; dinner etiquette Ren-and-Stimpy style.

49.desc: Ren and Stimpy are snowed in. Stimpy amuses himself with watching dark TV, whistling in a bottle and other mundane activities. / Ren and Stimpy are watching TV when they see the grand opening of a new jail where the prisoners are treated like kings.

50.desc: Stimpy gets paranoid because he's used up eight of his lives and only has one left to live. / Ren and Stimpy begin a job working for the Reverend Jack Cheese in his meat mobile.

51.desc: Stimpy believes in Yaksmas, yet Ren who thinks Yaksmas is stupid, doesn't believe in the festive holiday.

52.sub: Sammy and Me / The Last Temptation
52.desc: Stimpy's Sammy Mantis Jr. fan club kit arrives in the mail and Stimpy is overjoyed. Ren has a near death experience and is shown the error of his ways.

1.sub: The Crab with the Golden Claws: Part 1
1.desc: Tintin finds himself in the middle of a mystery involving a drowned man, a tin of crab meat, and a piece of paper with the name Karaboudjan on it. He follows the clues to a ship by the same name and finds its crew is using the crab tins to smuggle opiates out of the country, and all under the nose of the ship's drunken captain Haddock.

2.sub: The Crab with the Golden Claws: Part 2
2.desc: After Tintin & Haddock successfully escape from the Karaboudjan, they now find themselves lost in a desert. After passing out from the long walk through the vast hot sand they were rescued by an army that is stationed at a fort. After receiving water and camels for transportation, Tintin and Haddock head towards the nearest town. While they're there, Haddock discovers that the Karaboudjan is there only under a different name while Tintin discovers that Alan the Skipper who is leader of the crew's drug business is present in town. The only way to stop the mutiny crew is by finding the kingpin of the operations and Alan is Tintin's only link in finding the base of their operations.

3.sub: The Secret of the Unicorn: Part 1
3.desc: Tintin gets more than he bargained for when he buys a model of a sailing ship for Capt. Haddock that the seaman finds is unexpectedly familiar.

4.sub: The Secret of the Unicorn: Part 2
4.desc: Tintin and Captain Haddock learn there are violent rivals who are after the treasure of the Unicorn themselves.

5.desc: Tintin and the Captain search for the pirate's treasure they learned about the last story ("The Secret of the Unicorn"), with the help of their eccentric, but lovable new friend, Professor Calculus

6.desc: While on vacation in Egypt, Tintin is accused of drug smuggling and later becomes the target of a secret society.

7.desc: After learning about the opium being smuggled from India, Tintin heads over there in a plane he stole from an Arabic army that was in cahoots with the syndicate. Once he arrives there, he encounters Dr. Sarcophagus and asked him what has happened to him. Unfortunately the doctor isn't himself and is suffering from a poison that causes a him to go mad and not be able to think straight. Tintin had no choice but to seek medical help for the doctor, only to discover that there are syndicate members out to get rid of him.

8.desc: After the arrest of most of the members of the drug syndicate, the leader behind the organization was never found and is still at large. Tintin, who is enjoying his stay at the palace of the Maharaja, is visited by a Chinese gentleman who brings Tintin a message. However, a poison dart containing the madness poison was struck right into the massager's neck by an unseen marksman. The only clues Tintin received from the now mad messenger is that there's trouble in Shanghai and a man named Mitsuhirato, which is the place where the remaining members of the syndicate remain. So Tintin heads for Shanghai to meet Mitsuhirato, however upon meeting the person Tintin was almost assassinated twice upon his visit in Shanghai. He ends up being saved by a young Chinese man who provides him with a disguise in order for him to not be easily recognized by the syndicate. Who is the mysterious young man who prevented Tintin's death and can Mitsuhirato be trusted?

9.desc: The only way to save those who have been injected with the madness poison is by finding a doctor who can provide an antidote to cure them. However the doctor was kidnapped by the syndicate and is now being held hostage in Hukow outside the border of Shanghai. To make matters more difficult, Mitsuhirato has ordered the Japanese army station at the border of Shanghai to arrest Tintin if seen trying to exit the border of Shanghai. Tintin, will have to try to escape from Shanghai and head for Hukow to save the doctor and put an end to the syndicate once and for all. As well as learning who the mysterious leader of the organization is.

10.desc: When Tintin is shot by the pilot of downed plane, he travels to Britain to uncover a sinister plot.

11.desc: Tintin, still wondering Britain investigates a mysterious island in Scotland.

12.desc: After a terrible storm overnight Tin Tin and the Captain become aware someone is trying to kill them.

13.desc: Tintin and Haddock set out to rescue Professor Calculus.

14.desc: Tintin investigates a strange meteor, that appears in the sky, one night.

15.desc: When a South American fetish is stolen and than reappears the next morning, Tintin investigates.

16.desc: Tintin arrives at the village of the Arumbayas and finds the long-lost explorer Ridgewell, who is believed to be dead for many years.

17.desc: A good turn Tintin does for an absent-minded sigillographer gets him involved in dangerous political intrigue in the Balkan nation of Syldavia.

18.desc: Tintin and Snowy must recover the lost scepter of King Ottokar before the rightful King of Syldavia is forced to abdicate by enemy forces.

19.desc: When Tintin learns that his friend, Chang (from "The Blue Lotus") was in a plane crash in the Himalayas. Tintin, Snowy, and Captain Haddock go on the dangerous and somewhat impossible journey to find him.

20.desc: The sherpas escorting Tintin's party abandons them out of fear for the Abominable Snowman, the Yeti, all except Tharkey.

21.desc: Tintin walks into a dangerous trap after three of his friends are falsely arrested in South America.

22.desc: Tintin gets caught up in a South America trying to rescue his friends.

23.desc: When cars start exploding in their home country and it leads to a soon-to-be serious oil crisis. Tintin, along with Thompson and Thomson travel to the Middle East to get to the bottom of the situation.

24.desc: While trying to solve a mysterious oil crisis, Tintin uncovers a diabolical plot to start a world war.

25.desc: Tintin becomes caught up in the kidnapping of a millionaire.

26.desc: While trying to rescue a kidnapped millionaire, Tintin receives help from an unlikely source.

27.desc: Tintin and Captain Haddock travel to Khemed to rescue the Emir from the danger of arms smugglers who have overthrown his government.

28.desc: Tintin and Captain Haddock try to stop a terrible refugee smuggling ring and end up trapped with the other prisoners out at sea.

29.desc: Strange things begin happening to a group of archaeologists who have just returned from a exhibition to Peru.

30.desc: Tintin and captain Haddock discover that Professor Calculus has been kidnapped.

31.desc: Tintin and the Captain travel to Peru in search of Professor Calculus.

32.desc: In search for the prisoners and Professor Calculus, Tintin and Captain Haddock head for the "Temple of the Sun".

33.desc: After Capt. Haddock and Tintin invite an abused Roma community to camp on the grounds of Marlinspike, things get still more complicated when Bianca Castafiore and her entourage arrive as well.

34.desc: When Bianca Castafiore's prized jewel disappears, the Roma camped on the grounds of Marlinspike are suspected while Tintin secretly investigates the situation.

35.desc: Tintin and his friends join Professor Calculus' top secret space program in Syldavian.

36.desc: Tintin and Captain Haddock have been asked to be part of the expedition to the moon. As they help Professor Calculus prepare for the launch, Tintin persists in finding the internal spy.

37.desc: On Professor Calculus's nuclear powered rocket, Tintin and his friends travel to the moon, but there is trouble aboard.

38.desc: Tintin, Captain Haddock, Calculus, the Thompsons' and Wolff uncover the wonders of the moon. They also discover another person aboard the rocket ship who threatens to leave them all stranded on the moon.

39.desc: Tintin goes to 1930s Chicago to write about the organized crime-wave and ends up helping the police take down the infamous Al Capone and his gang!

1.desc: Marc learns that his mother is coming which explained why most of its inhabitants don't want to be around when she arrives.

2.desc: Marc teaches the importance of taking care of your teeth. Marc shows us we can recycle gum after we chewed it with the "Gum Again Machine" and shows us interesting chewed gum art work.

3.desc: A huge heat wave hits Weinerville as everyone tries to stay cool.

4.desc: While cleaning up Schnitzel's poop, Marc is called by Mayor Dottie to help get Zip out of the vacuum cleaner.

5.desc: Zip plays on a toy rocketship and is accidentally launched into outer space. Marc and Mayor Dottie enlist Captain Ozone to help rescue Zip.

6.desc: Mayor Dottie enlists a detective named Nick Tracy to find the missing cartoons.

7.desc: A giant spider has caught Zip.

8.desc: Marc learns from Mayor Dottie that ghosts have been haunting Weinerville.

9.desc: After Marc overeats and becomes fat, Dottie puts him on a vigorous exercise program.

10.desc: Marc starts a football team as Big Pops, Mayor Dottie, and Socko want to be on it as the quarterback.

11.desc: Zip gets stuck in the VCR as Mayor Dottie works to get him out.

12.desc: Mayor Dottie has a magic kit and she has to use instructions. She zapped Zip too many times, but she can't stop waving with her wand.

13.desc: Upon seeing Mayor Dottie's bubblegum-blowing trophies, Zip starts blowing bubblegum and starts getting trapped.

14.desc: Weinerville is holding a talent show where Big Pops plays the kazoo with his nose, Marc juggles, and Dottie does a mime act. However, Captain Bob's drums and hula girl wins.

15.desc: It's Mayor Dottie's birthday as Marc tries to find her a good birthday present.

16.desc: Big Pops makes his special spaghetti and meatballs which everyone wants to try as he demonstrates how he makes it.

17.desc: The citizens of Weinerville are baking cakes in order to raise money for the Old Puppets Home.

18.desc: Mayor Dottie gets some balloons from Nick Tracy (who was last seen in "Missing Cartoons"). When Zip asks Mayor Dottie for a balloon, he gets stuck on one of them. Meanwhile, Pops and Louie have an argument on who has been belching smoke near their buildings.

19.desc: Zip takes an interest in joining Weinerville's baseball team, while practicing his batting. Marc has been getting tired of Schnitzel's jokes that he tells the audience to test there hand eye coordination by focusing on throwing baseballs at a target, like Schnitzel.

20.desc: Mayor Dottie gets a call from the Head of the Network that there is going to be some budget cutbacks.

21.desc: Zip cooks up some popcorn. However, he uses way too much and the whole Puppet City is covered in popcorn.

22.desc: Everyone in Weinerville does their part in recycling.

23.desc: It's snowing in Puppet City, Little Pops shovels all his snow to Louie's door, closing him in.

24.desc: Zip rides a train in Dottie's office, but it goes out of control and Zip goes crashing through the wall. Marc has his own train with a couple children from the audience, and tells them to smile and wave and makes a ratings joke.

25.desc: Dottie puts together a seance to connect with the spirit of Zip's great grandfather to find out where his family treasure is buried. Things however keep on interrupting her.

26.desc: The Ziggy Zag Concert is occurring in Weinerville.

27.desc: Baby Jeffrey is going to camp and Dottie was nice and packed for him. But Dottie packed too many suitcases and has to repack due to rules.

28.desc: Dottie can't watch TV, her auxiliary satellite is on the fritz. So she calls for Captain Ozone to try and fix it.

29.desc: Professor Phosphate's rats escaped from his lab and are all over puppet city.

43.desc: Dottie and Commander Ozone switch bodies in a Freaky Friday fashion.

47.desc: Dottie has been invited to her high school reunion. Not particularly excited, she invites Socko as her date and makes a great impression.

49.desc: Weinerville is being sued by a Spanish show called "Weinervilla" claiming "Weinerville" stole their idea.

53.desc: Dottie is no longer the mayor of Weinerville. She'll become a producer of her own cable channel called DTV. Many are called cartoons and talk shows. What will happen is Marc wasn't pleased?

56.desc: Zip gets fed up with Dottie and quits his job.

you can t do that on television 1979.display: You Can't Do That on Television (1979)

1.desc: Kids from Ottawa offer up phone-in giveaways, comedy skits, and community events on a live show.

2.desc: Amid disco dancing, call-in contests, and community announcements, Tim has numerous difficulties in trying to attract Cindy's interest.

3.desc: While Kevin Somers lets his new TV fame go directly to his head, Jono learns how to broadcast the weather through buckets of rain, snow, and hail on his head.

4.desc: Sketch-TV by young amateur actors in true classic Nick-style. Whatever you do, never ask for water or admit that you don't know.

5.desc: The kids exercise on a stationary bike and use the TV station's special effects to create changes of scenery; while trying to stay healthy and exercise, the kids' efforts are halted by the adults; the boy escapes by going jogging with the firing squad.

6.desc: Tim is in the dungeon and is told not to pull the chains. He does not listen and gets slimed.

7.desc: On St. Patrick's Day, amid disco-dancing finalists, call-in contests, and community announcements, Lisa sets out to get Bradfield wearin' green--slime, that is.

8.desc: Sketch-TV by young amateur actors in true classic Nick-style. Whatever you do, never ask for water or admit that you don't know.

9.desc: Amidst disco dancing and call-in contests, the kids plot to pie and slime one another while Mr. Dime has the executive-washroom locks changed.

10.desc: The kids present the usual live jokes and call-in contests, along with filmed segments showing Ottawa children and teens telling their own jokes, classroom sketches, disruptions in the library, mock executions, and kid-and-parent interactions. Music videos and disco dancers, hosted by Jim Johnson, are seen about every 10 minutes. Standard features of the series include the locker jokes, cream pies in the face, and green slime for anyone who says, "I don't know" for any reason.

11.desc: The TV station producing the show has ordered that everyone in the studio on weekends must wear a straitjacket.

12.desc: Sketch-TV by young amateur actors in true classic Nick-style. Whatever you do, never ask for water or admit that you don't know.

13.desc: The kids who usually do the show in a studio are "on location" in Ottawa, highlighting a walkathon in aid of charity, interviewing various participants who have gathered sponsors for their attempt at the 50 km walk.

14.desc: The show is ending its first season as a local program, and the cast members wonder if they'll be picked up by the national network in the next season.

15.desc: Christine demonstrates workmanship by shoveling dirt onto a wheelbarrow on the set.

16.desc: The topic of transportation inspires conversations about cars, buses and airplane luggage while it grants Ross a special power by which to bother Christine.

17.desc: Christine decides to go on strike.

18.desc: The show finds Christine keeping vigilance by the studio phone in hopes that Nigel, her supposed boyfriend, will call.

19.desc: For the show topic of fitness, Christine rides her exercise bike while Ross tries ways to get a family allowance check.

20.desc: With safety in mind, Christine advises viewers to be careful and mindful of many hazardous objects and situations (with redundant emphasis placed on wearing white at night).

21.desc: With equality at issue, Brodie, Rodney and Lisa demand Christine share her hosting duties with them. Her easy agreement sounds like sweet victory till pies, normally destined for Christine, start flying their way.

22.desc: The subject of personal cleanliness inspires Christine to host the show while soaking luxuriously in her own bubble-filled bathtub.

23.desc: The subject of smoking has the kids mostly ridiculing it for its foul smell and threat to health while trying to get some adults to quit.

24.desc: The theme is juvenile crime and punishment with the set suffering a long, slow disappearance of equipment, personal apparel and, eventually, personnel.

25.desc: Self-splatting pie addicts abound to comically lampoon the foolishness of drug addiction.

26.desc: The show supports the position that healthy foods are good to eat, while junk foods are good for raising pimple farms.

27.desc: For a show on Peer Pressure, two Peers from England's House of Lords come to belly-bump Christine while Kevin Schenk feels the pressure after he and Rodney drop a pier on his foot.

28.desc: The show explores those things which enhance a person's physical appeal, such as makeup, deodorant, breath spray, beauty cream, perfumes and aftershave, and the like.

29.desc: The cast prides itself on avoiding the addictions of its parent generation but displays a variety of addictions all their own.

30.desc: Ross starts an audience survey to determine who's most popular on the show, and the kids talk themselves into believing that the winner gets his or her own dressing room.

31.desc: With her castmates following an ever-changing stream of fashion trends, Christine manages to remain always a step behind the times.

32.desc: For the show's theme on vacations, Christine decides to get away and lay out at the beach, but that doesn't stop Ross and others from finding her.

33.desc: The studio is one year old, but it's not a time to celebrate. The warranty has expired and now all the studio equipment is suddenly in danger of malfunctioning and falling apart.

34.desc: To prepare herself against bullies, Christine dons her gi to practice karate moves, but that won't stop the usual pitfalls of being the host or the relentless little terror that is Alasdair Gillis.

35.desc: The show lays out a feast of classic cultural elements, highlighting the Bard, opera, ballet, and portrait painting.

36.desc: Christine shares the chaos, romance, support, terminology, water, and slime that go into, around, and about the production of their TV show.

37.desc: Christine and Lisa jacket themselves as sportscasters to lead the show in a sports-angled view of the world.

38.desc: Superheroes, hero-types and those in real life we look up to get the comedic skewer as the cast touches the many whom kids or society chose to admire.

39.desc: It's not fair. That's the cry of foul play with a look at, or whines about, unfairness. Adding to the misery is an Un-Fairy-Godmother who keeps granting wishes in the worst possible ways.

40.desc: A look at fears and growing up.

41.desc: The show targets television and newspaper medias, mainly for their deceptiveness in advertising. Living the example, the show calls itself "new and improved" but admits having little to show for it.

42.desc: The show's theme on pets prompts Lisa to aim an endless stream of derisive dog jokes at Christine, which puts Christine in mind for revenge.

43.desc: Laughter is the best medicine for what ails you, but this "Medicine" show deals almost exclusively with ailments alone.

44.desc: Having discovered kids working for "You Can't Do That On Television", the government imposes new rules and regulations to protect them. First rule: since money corrupts, the kids can't be paid.

45.desc: To peer into the future, Christine consults her horoscope, dusts off her crystal ball, shuffles her Tarot cards, traces her lifeline and devours her fortune cookies - but still can't see to avoid the slime coming her way.

46.desc: Catch fish, dry fish, pitch a tent, make fire with two sticks. The gang all take a stab at getting back to nature through camping, but their lack of woods savvy is abundantly evident.

47.desc: It's a toss-up over who's better as Lisa and Christine pit their questionable culinary skills in a cooking throw-down, relying upon unwary cast members to judge between the lesser gastronomic evils of their unsavory creations.

48.desc: The kids cry "age discrimination" over all instances and situations that run contrary to meeting their desires.

49.desc: When the nameplate and star disappear from Christine's dressing room door, and her key no longer fits the lock, word spreads that she's being fired.

50.desc: As the gang tackles the world of classical music, Christine struggles to play the cello like a violin, figuring they look the same so they should be played the same. Invariably, it all goes to prove that music for some is noise to others.

51.desc: Habitual bad manners (a.k.a. disgusting habits) get the focus as Christine consults the questionable Book of Etiquette compiled by the show's producers.

52.desc: Kevin seeks fame, starting off by giving himself the new stage name of Kevin Illyanovich Rasputin Kubusheskie, which could get him fired for putting the show over its ink budget in trying to write it out.

53.desc: Christine questions Ross' priorities when he cancels the show to go to a baseball game, but a few choice words from the producer changes his attitude.

54.desc: The kids discuss courage. Kevin tests his courage by wearing a suit of armor.

55.desc: You can't put a price tag on friendship. Well, in fact, you can, as Christine sadly discovers when her mother's monthly friendship checks to the cast fail to arrive, leaving her friendless.

56.desc: Christine wants to grow as an actress and begs Ross to provide her with a meaty scene within the show. Ben, meanwhile, wants Ross to adjust the budget so he can star in his own music video.

57.desc: Christine starts her new favorite hobby by trading Ross' rare coin collection for an exercise bike and a set of free weights.

58.desc: Explores the paranormal, a poltergeist invades the studio (sending equipment and personnel flying), Lisa conducts séances, and a thankful genie freed from an electric lamp grants wishes.

59.desc: A show on literature inspires Christine to become a writer. Meanwhile, Justin sets out to expose history's cover-up of the world's most prolific writer--A. Nonymous--whom he believes to be the true author of Shakespeare's works.

60.sub: Clubs
60.desc: Christine joins a fitness club for its tennis outfits, restaurant, tan and muscular guys, and fashion show; Ross involves the kids in an investment club with himself as their broker.

61.desc: With a multitude of family vacations to foreign countries coming up, Ross seizes every opportunity to shortchange the kids in exchanging their dollars for foreign currency.

62.desc: The kids try to find something to market for the show so it does not get axed.

63.desc: As Alasdair's exploration of his family tree starts connecting him with castmates, Ross fears that the kids will start making fun of his age, so he conducts a preemptive strike.

64.desc: The producer has Ross check through the cast for a perfect body-type to be featured in an upcoming commercial. The kids look upon this as a stepping-stone for one of them to become a star but haven't a clue what body-type is being sought.

65.desc: Ross installs an audience interactive mechanism which can influence the outcomes of various scenes, but Christine discovers it can, more importantly, bring about the silencing of Motormouth Lisa.

66.desc: While Christine's family moves to an upscale neighborhood (which eventually proves too ritzy for their other-than-blue blood), a kid on wheels from California catches the attention of his new classmates.

67.desc: When Ross openly disdains Halloween, Christine invokes a pretend spell to mess with his head. He's not impressed, but when a continuous string of accidents and near disasters enters his life, he's ready to admit she's a bone fide witch.

68.desc: It's Christmas on the set, but there's little peace on Earth in the studio: Alasdair's running around with a helmet camouflaged in mistletoe and two eager lips puckered.

69.desc: The kids rally for an Actors' Holiday so they can have a day off just to be kids, but Ross abhors the idea.

70.desc: Among the cast's plans for college, Alasdair plans to enter on a video game scholarship but, so far, can't find a university to meet his aim. Ross returns to college so he can enter a profession without kids around.

71.desc: Christine decides that Lisa has what it takes to run for class president: a boring, uneventful background; an uncle who can supply voters with free pizzas; and a mouth that can talk on and on without saying anything.

72.desc: While the group has a field day with botany, chemistry, and physics, Alasdair discovers the formula for green slime and announces his findings to the viewing public.

73.desc: During their divorce proceedings, the producer's wife takes half the show away--literally half of everything--with strange results.

74.desc: Ross' nephew Jeff joins the cast but his family ties spare him from the usual punishments endured by the other cast members, who resent this.

75.desc: The kids hang out--at the arcade, the library, malls, summer camp, after school, at the Burgery, around the set, outside prison, stores, and locker and dressing rooms. They also hang laundry, hang tough, and generally just hang in there.

76.desc: Alasdair brings his weather machine to the studio. The crazy thing works but has no off switch and its selector malfunctions.

77.desc: Ross wears his old army uniform in protest of the kids' griping about war. Meanwhile, Alasdair starts a peace movement called "War's Insane: Make Peace" (W.I.M.P.).

78.desc: When Christine gets a raise in salary, the rest of the cast gets jealous.

79.desc: To meet budget requirements for an episode on wealth, the producer markets it to investors. Unfortunately, once they see the product they're buying into, the production goes back up for sale.

80.desc: Doug plans a trip to outer space.

81.desc: While half the cast takes the theme of animals and wildlife to mean the party-animal lifestyle of punk rockers, a blow to the head leaves Alasdiar thinking he's a dog.

82.desc: Alistair tries to set a world record for eating the most hard boiled eggs.

83.desc: The cast tries answering the question "Just who do you think you are?"

84.desc: Alasdair, hosting this show on optimism and pessimism, thinks it will be great, but Christine, who has read the script, thinks otherwise.

85.desc: Lisa receives letters from an unknown secret admirer.

86.desc: The cast deals with fears, phobias, and a few hidden monsters.

87.desc: In a show centered around blood relations and ancestry, Barth leaves relatives in change while on vacation, and Ross charges the cast to research their family trees.

88.desc: As everyone becomes vengeance-minded, Alasdair tries to put Ross' box of Instant Revenge to use, and the somewhat-inept Masked Revenger avails his transformation superpower to address the grievances of the disgruntled.

89.desc: A big-time Hollywood producer plans to make a major motion-picture version of the show, and the kids go through slime-wrenching auditions just to get parts.

90.desc: The kids discuss fairy tales and Alasdair tries to become a wizard.
